steps.text: Combine strawberries, pineapple juice, milk, yogurt, sugar, and wheat germ in a blender; add ice. Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides of the jar as needed.

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry-Pineapple Smoothie
raw_recipe.description: Smoothie lovers will enjoy this healthy recipe of pineapple juice, strawberries, vanilla yogurt, milk, and wheat germ for a refreshing and healthy treat.
raw_recipe.name: Strawberry-Pineapple Smoothie

recipeInstructions.text: Combine strawberries, pineapple juice, milk, yogurt, sugar, and wheat germ in a blender; add ice. Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides of the jar as needed.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! I used fresh strawberries and fresh pineapple chunks instead and it came out so yummy. Thank you for the recipe.

Wow! Tasted so good I decided to add more ice and make popsicles. Didn't have pineapple juice so I used fresh pineapple. Also, I used the wheat germ and 1 T flax seed. After I got the kidlets' portion out, I added a few handful if frozen swiss chard to make my green smoothie. The pineapple did well in covering the swiss chard taste. Awesome recipe and a definite keeper!

oh wow is this good!!! I am a smoothie girl. Smoothies are that rare edible that can be as healthy (and still delicious) as you want or can be just pure sugar and satisfy that craving you have for something "bad for you." This one fits both bills at the same time. I used frozen strawberries, a small can of crushed pineapple, plain unflavored yogurt (and I added a splash of vanilla to compensate), skipped the ice cubes (its the middle of winter and I am tast-testing smoothie recipes to make up a recipe book for all my nieces for Christmas and I actually like thick smoothies and without the ice cubes this was the perfect consistency to me)and added 1 T ground flax seed which makes every smoothie good for me!!! LOVE IT!!!

Very tasty! I changed it up a fair bit - I used pineapple chunks instead of pineapple juice, added a full scoop of vanilla whey protein, and added a lot of ice; also I left out the sugar, b/c if you have all that fruit and yogurt, it's sweet enough for my taste. Came out very well, though next time I will add more ice for a thicker texture.

Very good. It didn't get a 5 star because I didn't use all the ingredients. I didn't add the sugar, because it was sweet enough for me. I also didn't add the ice cubes. Plus I left out the wheat germ.

The milk I used was almond milk, the yogurt was technically Honey flavored and I used about 1 cup of frozen pineapple chunks instead of juice. Didn't do the extra sugar, did do the wheat germ. This was light, refreshing and perfect. I was looking for a smoothie that wasn't chunky or have bits to chew and also wasn't super sweet. This was it :)

I changed the recipe a little because I like my smoothies thick. I also changed the servings to 5. I used a cup of greek strawberry yogurt and did not add the milk, and I used one 20oz can of pineapples in natural juice. The kids loved it and so did I.

I changed it up just a tad. I had a large amout of fresh sliced pineapple, so I used pineapple in place of pineapple juice. I also used fresh strawberries in place of frozen and skipped the ice cubes as I am not an "icy" kinda smoothie person, I like it smooth and fresh. I have wheat germ, so I used it in my smoothies. It turned out excellent and I will make this again!
This is delicious! I found the sugar to be unnecessary. The smoothies are plenty sweet enough with just the pineapple juice and vanilla yogurt.
I used a cup of fresh pineapple instead of the juice and left out the sugar! Very good!

I'll be honest and say I didn't even try the recipe as is. I didn't have pineapple juice or vanilla yogurt. What I did have was a good portion of a 20 oz. can of pineapple tidbits with juice and vanilla bean ice cream. I used the exact same measured amounts for both - as called for in the original recipe. I omitted the ice since I used the frozen strawberries and vanilla ice cream. (Wheat germ was out of the question. This drink was all about the yumminess factor and not the nutritional value.) They turned out AMAZING! Sure, it's more of a milkshake at that point, but still a yummy treat. Even my toddlers loved it and asked for seconds. Use the servings adjustment tool if you need more than two servings. In my case I needed enough for six!
It's good but will be better with frozen pineapple chunks. No pineapple juice or wheat germ.
I thought this was delicious. I omitted the wheat germ only because I don't have any. Other than that I followed the recipe. Super refreshing and extremely tasty. Thanks for the recipe!
I doubled the recipe to make 4 cups instead of 2 It was delicious family approved great recipe😋👍
This recipe was simple and tasty. I did not have pineapple juice just used fresh pineapple everything else was the same. Very good. Will definitely make again. Thanks
Made a few slight tweaks. Kids loved it!
Use frozen pineapples.
What a cool, refreshing smoothie! I didn't add the ice since the strawberries were frozen, nor did I add the sugar. It was plenty sweet for me. A delicious way to start the day!
better taste with more pineapple (not juice of course)

Used frozen pineapple instead of juice and ice cubes. Plain yogurt, a little vanilla extract, and Splenda instead of sugar. Not much flavor. Would have been better with vanilla yogurt ( per the original recipe) and more pineapple.
